## 1. Summary

<!--# 
With a maximum of 300 words, describe the indicator in general terms as you would to a non-expert. Think of this as a kind of common language summary. Follow the four numbers sub-headers below. under point 2, it is possible under  include a bullet point list of the specific steps in the workflow. 
 -->

1. **Background and rationale**:
The eelgrass index (Ålegressindeks) is a biological indicator used to assess ecological condition in Norwegian coastal waters under the Water Framework Directive and the Norwegian Water Regulation. The indicator is based on eelgrass (Zostera marina), a habitat-forming marine angiosperm that occurs on soft bottom in sheltered coastal and fjord environments where macroalgal indicators are often absent. Eelgrass meadows are important habitats for many marine animals including juvenile fish. They are also sensitive to eutrophication, reduced water transparency and increased growth of filamentous algae, making them effective indicators of environmental degradation.  

2. **Methods**:
The indicator combines three components of eelgrass condition: lower depth limit, meadow density and degree of epiphytic algal overgrowth. Lower depth limit reflects water clarity and light availability, density reflects meadow integrity, and overgrowth reflects eutrophication-related stress. Each component is converted to a score based on reference conditions and class boundaries defined for Norwegian coastal ecoregions and water types. The final Ecological Quality Ratio (EQR) is calculated as a weighted index where depth limit contributes 50%, density 30% and overgrowth 20%. EQR values range from 0 to 1, where higher values indicate better ecological condition.


3. **Interpretation**:
<!-- Add a very short description of how the indicator values should be interpreted. Here's an example for a bumblebee indicator: An indicator value of 1 signifies an intact bumblebee community. Values decreasing toward zero reflect negative ecological change, specifically the decline of species expected to be present. This metric does not account for potentially positive changes, such as increases in species' abundance or the arrival of new species. Tip: Add text on the line directly following the subheader, and don't introduce blank lines. This way the whole paragraph renders as a block quote. -->
An EQR value close to 1 indicates eelgrass meadows with near-reference depth distribution, high density and little algal overgrowth. Lower values indicate increasing deviation from reference conditions, typically associated with eutrophication, reduced light penetration and habitat degradation.  

4. **Results and development needs**:
<!-- Briefly, what does the indicator say about the ecosystem condition. What is the current status of  the metric (can it be used or is it still in development), and what immediate tasks remain to improve the indicator or to make the indicator operational -->
The current implementation uses Vannmiljø monitoring data from the Økokyst (and Oslofjord??) reference stations and provides a transparent and reproducible workflow for calculating eelgrass EQR values. Future development should focus on broader geographic coverage, automated linkage to national typology datasets and formal uncertainty estimation.

## 2. About the underlying data

<!--# Give a general introduction the datasets you have used, and provide more specific details in the sub-chapters.  -->

Data are obtained from Vannmiljø observations originating primarily from Økokyst monitoring activities. Observations are recorded at individual monitoring stations and sampling dates. The current implementation includes repeated measurements from multiple years at fixed eelgrass locations.

### 2.1 Spatial and temporal resolution and extent

<!--# Describe the temporal and spatial resolution and extent of the data used -->

Eelgrass meadows occur as distinct patches in the marine environment. Measurements of ecological status is collected at a limited number of selected eelgrass meadows, here denoted as monitoring stations. The monitoring stations are fixed and data for the stations are collected once every year or less frequently.  


### 2.2 Sampling design

<!-- How was the data sampled? Describe potential sampling biases -->

#### Measurements in the field  

Surveys are conducted from small boats using underwater video equipment with an integrated depth sensor. Monitoring follows protocols developed for Norwegian coastal ecosystem monitoring and the Water Framework Directive. The observations used by the indicator are collected along a set of standardized transects designed to capture variation in the lower depth limit of eelgrass meadows, eelgrass density, and algal overgrowth throughout the meadow.

At each monitoring station, observations are made along one transect following the shoreline and an additional 5–10 transects extending from shallow water to slightly below the lower depth limit of the eelgrass meadow. Along these transects, point observations are recorded using an underwater camera, while all positions are georeferenced using GPS. The approach is intended to provide representative coverage of the entire eelgrass meadow, including both the shallow portions and the deepest occurrence of eelgrass.

The lower depth limit used in the indicator corresponds to the lower depth limit of the eelgrass meadow rather than the deepest individual plant. Following the national methodology, the lower meadow limit is defined as the deepest observation classified as sparse eelgrass (density class 2). This definition is intended to provide a robust and repeatable estimate of the depth distribution of the meadow.

Eelgrass density and epiphytic algal overgrowth are recorded at all observation points along the shoreline transect and the offshore transects. Both variables are classified using a four-level ordinal scale similar to that employed in the Norwegian National Programme for Mapping Biodiversity in Coastal Waters. Eelgrass density ranges from isolated plants to dense, continuous meadows, while overgrowth ranges from little or no epiphyte cover to dominant algal overgrowth.

To ensure comparability among stations and years, all depth measurements are corrected for water level variation using information on tides, wind conditions, and atmospheric pressure. This standardization reduces variation caused by short-term changes in sea level and allows ecological changes in eelgrass depth distribution to be assessed more consistently over time.

Detailed descriptions of field procedures, point selection criteria, and calculation rules are provided in Trannum et al. (2022).


### 2.3 Original units

<!--# What are the original units for the most relevant  variables in the data-->

**The lower depth limit** is recorded in meters (m).  

**Eelgrass density** is measeured on a 4 level scale:  

| Level | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| 1 | Enkeltfunn (isolated plants) |
| 2 | Spredte planter (sparse meadow) |
| 3 | Flekkvis tett eng (patchy dense meadow) |
| 4 | Tett, heldekkende eng (continuous dense meadow) |

**Epiphytic algal overgrowth** is measured on a 4 level scale:

| Level | Observed category | Observed category (No) | Indicator score |
|------------------|----------------|----------------|
| 0 | No overgrowth | Ingen begroing | 4 |
| 1 | Little overgrowth | Lite begroing | 4 |
| 2 | Sparse overgrowth |  Spredt begroing | 3 |
| 3 | Common overgrowth | Vanlig begroing | 2 |
| 4 | Dominating overgrowth | Dominerende begroing | 1 |

The reference levels for the lower depth limit of the eelgrass meadow (i.e. the depth limit for under pristine conditions) depends on ecoregion and water type, as the light penetration varies under natural conditions.  


#### Calculation of nEQR  

The final Ecological Quality Ratio (EQR) is calculated as a weighted combination of the three component scores:

$$ nEQR = 0.5 \cdot D +  0.3 \cdot T +  0.5 \cdot B$$ {#eq-continuity}

where:

* *D* = depth-limit score (0–5),
* *T* = density score (1–4),
* *B* = overgrowth score (1–4).

The weights reflect the relative importance assigned in the national classification scheme, with lower depth limit contributing 50% of the final score, density 30%, and algal overgrowth 20%. The resulting EQR is bounded between 0 and 1 and provides a normalized measure of ecological condition. Higher values indicate eelgrass meadows that more closely resemble reference conditions.


The **depth limit score (D)** depends on eco-region and water type:

| Ecoregion | Water type | Score 5 | Score 4 | Score 3 | Score 2 | Score 1 | Score 0 |
|-----------|----------|----------|----------|----------|----------|----------|----------|
| Nordsjøen sør | 2 | > 8 m | > 6–8 m | > 5–6 m | > 3–5 m | > 2–3 m | 0–2 m |
| Nordsjøen sør | 3 | > 8 m | > 6–8 m | > 5–6 m | > 3–5 m | > 2–3 m | 0–2 m |
| Nordsjøen nord | 3 | > 7 m | > 6–7 m | > 4–6 m | > 3–4 m | > 1–3 m | 0–1 m |
| Norskehavet sør* | 3 | > 7 m | > 6–7 m | > 4–6 m | > 3–4 m | > 1–3 m | 0–1 m |

The **density score (T)** is equal to the density, measured on a scale from 1-4. 

The **overgrowth score (B)** is given as follows::

| Level | Observed category | Overgrowth score (B) |
|------------------|----------------|----------------|
| 0 | No overgrowth | 4 |
| 1 | Little overgrowth | 4 |
| 2 | Sparse overgrowth |  3 |
| 3 | Common overgrowth | 2 |
| 4 | Dominating overgrowth | 1 |

```{r add_station_metadata}
  left_join(
    station_lookup,
    by = "Vannlokalitetsnavn"
  ) %>%

    !is.na(okoregion)
  )

# eelgrass_wide_2 |> head(3)

```

The calculation of nEQR is based on `Nedre voksegrense ålegresseng (takson)`, `Dekningsgrad ålegresseng (skala)`, and `Dekningsgrad marine begroingsalger (skala)`, as given in 
```{r calculate_nEQR}

# calculate nEQR for each station / year  
# 
eelgrass_eqr <- eelgrass_wide_2 %>%
  mutate(

    depth_score =
      get_depth_score(
        depth_limit,
        okoregion,
        vanntype
      ),

    density_score =
      get_density_score(density),

    epiphyte_score =
      get_epiphyte_score(epiphytes),

    nEQR =
      0.5 * (depth_score / 5) +
      0.3 * (density_score / 4) +
      0.2 * (epiphyte_score / 4),
    
    # for ordering in tables
    okoregion = factor(okoregion,
                       levels = c("Norskehavet sør", "Nordsjøen nord", "Nordsjøen sør"))
    
  )

# head(eelgrass_eqr, 2)

```

As an example, we show the measured values (depth_limit, density, epiphytes), the scores (depth_score, density_score, epiphyte_score), and the nEQR for three stations.  
```{r results_by_station_2025}

# results_by_station, 2025

eqr_table1 <- eelgrass_eqr |>
  filter(!is.na(nEQR) & year == 2024) |>
  select(Vannlokalitetsnavn, okoregion,
         depth_limit, density, epiphytes,
         depth_score, density_score, epiphyte_score, nEQR) |>
  arrange(okoregion)

head(eqr_table1, 3) |> 
  kable()

```

```{r results_by_station_allyears }
# 
# results by station, all years

eqr_table2 <- eelgrass_eqr |>
  select(Vannlokalitetsnavn, okoregion, year, nEQR) |>
  filter(!is.na(nEQR)) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = nEQR) |>
  arrange(okoregion, Vannlokalitetsnavn) 

# eqr_table2

```

Below, we show the mean score for each of the three criteria for each ecoregion as well as the mean of the resulting nEQR.
```{r results_by_ecoregion_2025}

# results_by_station, 2025

eqr_region <- eelgrass_eqr |>
  filter(!is.na(nEQR) & year == 2025) |>
  group_by(okoregion) |> 
  summarise(
    depth_score = mean(depth_score, na.rm = TRUE), 
    density_score = mean(density_score, na.rm = TRUE), 
    epiphyte_score = mean(epiphyte_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    nEQR = mean(nEQR, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  arrange(okoregion) 

eqr_region |> 
  kable()

```

## 10. Results

<!--# 

Repeat the final results here. Typically this is a map or table of indicator values.

This is typically where people will harvest data from, so make sure to include all relevant output here, but don't clutter this section with too much output either.

-->

The results by ecoregion for 2025 are shown below.

```{r}

eqr_region |> 
  select(okoregion, nEQR) |> 
  kable()  

```


Over all results (average) are:

```{r}

library(emmeans)
mod <- lm(nEQR ~ factor(year) + okoregion, data = eelgrass_eqr)
emmeans(mod, ~1, weights = "equal") |> 
  kable()  

```
